blocks.text: XS-Leaks infer otherwise unreadable cross-origin state through observable browser behavior such as load events, timing, framing and window relationships. The leak must distinguish a protected state, not merely identify that a URL exists.

items: Origin isolation and resource embedding policy gaps

blocks.text: Build a controlled target with two known states containing synthetic data and a separate probe origin. Use the same browser/version, network conditions and cookie policy for both controls. Repeat small, bounded samples, randomize state order and compare distributions before attributing a timing difference to secret state. Most snippets below are independent fixtures, not universally working leaks.

Browser restrictions may suppress events, timing details, cookies or frame access. That is a valid negative result. Resource Timing fields require the relevant Timing-Allow-Origin permissions; missing detail is not evidence of secret data. Do not use CORS access to read a response and call that an XS-Leak. Demonstrate the protected inference without reading the response body.

See `xs-leaks-payloads.txt` for browser snippets and test sequences. Replace the local fixture routes and select one probe at a time. Window creation may require a user gesture. Console output uses synthetic markers only.
